key_insight: GenEHR uses longitudinal health records to identify cohorts at elevated cancer risk, rather than discover cancer drugs.
clinical_relevance: If prospectively validated, GenEHR-CancerRisk could help prioritize high-risk patients for screening and prevention, including for pancreatic and ovarian cancers.
method: Train an autoregressive generative model on EHRs from millions of patients across diverse health systems.
Model diagnoses, medications, lab values, procedures, and irregular intervals between visits.
Apply parameter-efficient supervised adaptation to predict first cancer diagnoses across 17 cancer types within five years.
evidence_signal: Retrospective evaluation in five large EHR cohorts found substantially improved prediction performance after supervised adaptation; the abstract provides no numerical performance estimates.
watch_item: Prospective validation is needed to establish clinical benefit before use in screening decisions.
paper_title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
